title: People With a Chip on Their Shoulder
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece examines the double-edged nature of having a 'chip on your shoulder' -- a felt history of being underestimated or unfairly passed over -- as both a motivational asset and a workplace liability. It notes that some leaders deliberately seek out chippy hires for their scrappiness and results orientation, but warns that the same sensitivity to past slights can trigger disproportionate reactions to mundane comments and turn into disruptive score-settling. The essay's practical takeaway is calibration: everyone carries some chip, but a chip that's clearly visible and easily triggered is a warning sign worth heeding in hiring and team management.
points: A 'chip on the shoulder' -- a felt history of being underestimated or unfairly passed over -- can motivate people to work harder and prove their value.
Some leaders deliberately hire chippy people for the scrappiness and results-orientation the chip produces.
The same sensitivity to past slights can cause chippy people to take outsized offense at mundane comments and try to settle perceived scores.
Everyone carries some chip; the real signal is whether it's visible enough that others can sense it.
A chip that is painfully obvious is a warning sign that a team member's reactions to everyday events may be hijacked by it, to the team's detriment.
quotes: Someone with a "chip" on their shoulder believes they have been underestimated, passed over, undervalued, or rejected unfairly.
In the view of many leaders, a chip, if channeled appropriately, can be a tremendous advantage in the workplace.
Those with a chip are expected to be highly results and outcome-oriented and to become team members who will do whatever it takes to get things done.
It is not uncommon for those with a chip to want to settle perceived scores by fighting through them.
Everyone has a chip on their shoulder about something. No one has traveled through life without being unfairly slighted or rejected along the way.
Chips come in all sizes, shapes, and weights. If they are too heavy, they weigh people down.
